A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoVITA by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials support reliable comparison, including matching content across appendix reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, training ablations, grounding analyses, and qualitative results in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds task-category results, a teacher-choice experiment, inference measurements, and analysis of 3,278 training rollouts.

M1.justification: The planning-verification-answer procedure, SFT/GRPO training, ACMG reward, confidence reward, and exocentric regularization remain unchanged. The same-video verification language clarifies existing inputs; the alternative teacher is an experimental configuration, not a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v3 supplementary Table 4 newly evaluates Ego-Exo-Bench, extending evaluated cross-view benchmark coverage beyond its related-work citation in v2. Existing training datasets and benchmarks remain. The new task-category breakdowns subdivide already evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same foundation-model, SFT, sparse-reward GRPO, and EgoThinker baselines. The added benchmark uses existing comparators; the teacher-choice experiment varies EgoVITA rather than introducing a competing method.

E3.justification: v3 adds a Qwen3-VL-30B teacher condition, single-GPU efficiency measurements, and Gemini-3.1-Flash classification of 3,278 training rollouts. The reported total training budget changes from 47k to 52k, although constituent dataset counts remain unchanged; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: main Table 3 examines task-specific gains, supplementary RQ7 tests teacher dependence, and supplementary Section 3 quantifies planner, verifier, and grounding failures with a concrete example. Existing pooling, temporal-window, regularization, component, and teacher-warm-up ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The bootstrap 95% confidence-interval reporting and significance convention in main Table 1 remain unchanged. No new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is reported. Added rollout frequencies are new descriptive results.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–2 and matched existing ablations retain their scores, but v3 adds substantial category, teacher-choice, efficiency, and failure results. The new teacher condition reports EgoBlind 38.5, versus 37.4 with the original teacher; these are different conditions. Supplementary Table 4 adds Ego-Exo-Bench 34.6. The warm-up discussion corrects the mean gain from +2.1 to +2.9, while the clause-reward mean range changes from 0.67–0.69 to 0.68–0.71 despite retaining the plot.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and the mathematical definitions of the policy, objectives, and rewards are unchanged. Correcting the supplement's max-pooling equation reference from Equation 6 to Equation 8 is a cross-reference correction, not revised mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and state-of-the-art discussion revise the sample-efficiency claim from 47k to 52k training samples. The central planning-verification contribution, dense rewards, headline +7.7/+4.4 improvements, and exocentric-retention claims remain.

C2.justification: Compared with v2's predominantly successful examples, v3 substantially expands limitations by explaining incorrect-plan confirmation, outcomes beyond the temporal window, and static-feature rewards that the verifier can reinforce. It also interprets category-specific gains and teacher robustness, and develops adaptive-window and iterative-verification directions in the conclusion.

D1.justification: v3 discloses inference performance on one L40S GPU: 84.3 tokens/s, 0.6-second time to first token, and 0.1-second overhead. It identifies the alternative teacher and rollout-labeling model. Existing architecture and prompt details remain. The explicit future code/model/data release promise disappears, although the project URL remains; actual availability is not established.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Qwen2-VL reference and explicitly identifies it as EgoThinker's backbone. The related-work argument otherwise remains stable; numerous venue and bibliographic updates refer to works already cited in v2.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify same-video verification and anticipatory grounding, expand the conclusion, and correct numerical explanations and cross-references. The supplement gains independent numbering and moves the architecture section after qualitative and failure analyses. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds three tables and a failure-case figure, redraws Figure 1 with a revised illustrative plan, and updates several captions. Existing appendix plots, architecture table, and prompt displays are retained but redistributed and renumbered. The overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: The task-category and teacher-choice analyses strengthen supporting evidence, while the quantified failure analysis makes limitations more transparent than v2's successful examples alone. Same-video clarification and the corrected warm-up average improve precision. The overall gain is limited: rollout labels are automated, and the reported 69% rejection rate includes unsuccessful corrections, so it does not establish equivalent correction success.
